sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.

sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily, today.
sentences.zh: 这是今天的《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: In his latest negotiation with Democrats over the shutdown, President Trump stormed out of the meeting.
sentences.zh: 在与民主党人就政府停摆进行的最新谈判中，特朗普总统愤然离开了会议。

sentences.en: Why his strategy requires giving no ground and forcing Republican senators to stand with him, no matter the coSt. It's Thursday, January 10th.
sentences.zh: 为什么他的策略要求寸步不让，并迫使共和党参议员无论付出什么代价都要支持他？今天是1月10日，星期四。

sentences.en: Julie Davis.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's day 19 of the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 这是政府停摆的第19天。

sentences.en: How does this latest day of a shutdown begin?
sentences.zh: 这停摆的最新一天是如何开始的？

sentences.en: Well, this is the day after the president's big primetime address and the Democrats giving their response.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是在总统发表黄金时段重要演讲以及民主党人做出回应后的第二天。

sentences.en: And what we're beginning to see is the first glimmers of Republican senators being deeply uncomfortable with where they find themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到共和党参议员对他们所处的境地感到非常不安的最初迹象。

sentences.en: I spoke with Julie Davis from inside the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我在国会大厦内采访了朱莉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: So on Wednesday morning, we start to see that Senator Lisa Murkowski, Republican senator from Alaska, is ready to break with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 周三上午，我们开始看到来自阿拉斯加州的共和党参议员丽莎·穆尔科斯基准备与特朗普总统决裂。

sentences.en: The operations of the Department of the Interior and the National Park Service or the operations of
sentences.zh: 内政部和国家公园管理局的运作，或者

sentences.en: the IRS and whether or not tax refunds go out don't have anything to do with border security.
sentences.zh: 国税局的运作以及退税是否发放，这些都与边境安全毫无关系。

sentences.en: And she says, we need to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们需要让政府重新开门。

sentences.en: Federal workers are hurting.
sentences.zh: 联邦工作人员正在受苦。

sentences.en: Americans are going to be affected or are affected already.
sentences.zh: 美国民众将会受到影响，或者说已经受到了影响。

sentences.en: And this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: We just need to buy for keep the two issues, get the government open, and then we can keep negotiating.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要把这两个问题分开，让政府恢复运作，然后我们可以继续谈判。

sentences.en: But we don't need to hold up these six other departments at the same time that we are resolving these very important security issues.
sentences.zh: 但我们没必要在解决这些非常重要的安全问题的同时，扣住其他六个部门不放。

sentences.en: So break with the president and his strategy publicly.
sentences.zh: 所以她公开与总统及其策略决裂了。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she's not the first Republican who's come out and suggested this.
sentences.zh: 她并不是第一个站出来提出这种建议的共和党人。

sentences.en: Colorado's Republican Senator Cory Gardner is breaking with President Trump on the government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州共和党参议员科里·加德纳在政府停摆问题上也与特朗普总统产生了分歧。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, we started to see some cracks.
sentences.zh: 周末的时候，我们开始看到了一些裂痕。

sentences.en: People like Cory Gardner, the senator from
sentences.zh: 像科里·加德纳这样的人，这位来自

sentences.en: Colorado, who is up for re-election in 2020.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州的参议员，他将在2020年面临连任。

sentences.en: I hope that we can continue to fight for additional border security dollars.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能继续争取额外的边境安全资金。

sentences.en: That's what we need to do.
sentences.zh: 这是我们需要做的。

sentences.en: But I don't think shutting down the government's the right way to do it.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为让政府停摆是实现这一目标的正确方式。

sentences.en: We could reopen much of government where there's no dispute.
sentences.zh: 我们可以让政府中没有争议的大部分部门重新开门。

sentences.en: Senator Susan Collins of Maine.
sentences.zh: 缅因州的参议员苏珊·柯林斯。

sentences.en: Certain departments like ag, transportation, housing, interior.
sentences.zh: 像农业、交通、住房、内政等特定部门。

sentences.en: Let's get those reopened while the negotiations continue.
sentences.zh: 让我们在谈判继续的同时，让这些部门重新开门吧。

sentences.en: You know, most of these people are moderates who are relatively less inclined to be lockstep with the president anyway.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些人大多是温和派，他们本来就不太倾向于与总统保持完全一致。

sentences.en: And they want to say, OK, we can continue to argue over our differences over the wall.
sentences.zh: 他们想说，好吧，我们可以继续争论我们在边境墙问题上的分歧。

sentences.en: They just want for the rest of the government to be able to open while that debate plays out.
sentences.zh: 他们只是希望在辩论进行的同时，政府的其他部门能够恢复运作。

sentences.en: And Julie, by Wednesday morning, when Murkowski comes out and says she doesn't think the strategy is working, how widespread is that feeling among Republican senators?
sentences.zh: 朱莉，到周三早上，当穆尔科斯基出来说她认为这个策略行不通时，这种情绪在共和党参议员中有多普遍？

sentences.en: Well, it's still a pretty small group, but it's building.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这仍然是一个很小的群体，但正在壮大。

sentences.en: It's, you know, more people every day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每天都有更多的人加入。

sentences.en: And that is going in the wrong direction if you're the president, because when you're in a fight like this, unanimity is very important.
sentences.zh: 如果你是总统，这正朝着错误的方向发展，因为当你陷入这样的斗争时，团结一致非常重要。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are clear indications here that
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这里有明显的迹象表明

sentences.en: Republicans are starting to stray off of that.
sentences.zh: 共和党人开始偏离这一立场了。

sentences.en: So a small and seemingly manageable kind of rebellion for Trump, but something that would be worrisome for him.
sentences.zh: 所以这对特朗普来说是一场看似可控的小规模反叛，但对他来说也是令人担忧的事情。

sentences.en: Well, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: And not something that if you're the president, you can afford not to address.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你是总统，这绝不是你可以忽视的问题。

sentences.en: They'd already seen defections from House Republicans when the House voted last week to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 上周众议院投票决定让政府重新开门时，他们已经看到了众议院共和党人的倒戈。

sentences.en: And there was a deep sense at the White House that they needed to kind of buck up Republicans to make sure that they didn't start to get even more defections and an even
sentences.zh: 白宫有一种强烈的紧迫感，他们需要提振共和党人的士气，以确保他们不会开始出现更多的倒戈，从而在

sentences.en: weaker hand against the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 对抗民主党时处于更弱势的地位。

sentences.en: So how does the president do that exactly?
sentences.zh: 那么总统究竟是怎么做的呢？

sentences.en: So on Wednesday, the president decided to go to the Capitol to attend the weekly Senate Republican lunch to make the case himself in person, which is fairly rare.
sentences.zh: 周三，总统决定前往国会大厦参加每周一次的参议院共和党午餐会，亲自当面进行游说，这相当罕见。

sentences.en: And what exactly does it tell you, Julie, that the president is traveling to Congress, kind of to their terrain to do this?
sentences.zh: 朱莉，总统亲自前往国会，来到他们的地盘做这件事，这到底说明了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think it tells us that, you know, he's worried about losing support on this, that he knows
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这说明他担心在这件事上失去支持，他知道

sentences.en: that he has to give them something to rally around, because if he doesn't, he's going to be at risk of losing support on what has become a very politically difficult fight.
sentences.zh: 他必须给他们一些可以团结起来的东西，因为如果不这样做，他就有可能在这一场已经变得非常棘手的政治斗争中失去支持。

sentences.en: And also just that he really sees this as a public relations and messaging fight that he has to try to get out in front of.
sentences.zh: 而且这也说明他确实将此视为一场公共关系和舆论战，他必须努力争取主动权。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we know from our conversation with Senator Chuck Schumer last week, the Democratic minority
sentences.zh: 我们从上周与民主党少数党领袖查克·舒默参议员的谈话中得知，

sentences.en: leader, that this worry of Trump's is precisely the Democratic strategy, which is to peel off Republican
sentences.zh: 特朗普的这种担忧正是民主党的策略，即分化共和党

sentences.en: senators, get them to turn on the president and this shutdown strategy by separating the issue of the wall from the funding of the government.
sentences.zh: 参议员，通过将边境墙问题与政府拨款问题分开，让他们转而反对总统和这种停摆策略。

sentences.en: What the president fears is exactly what the Democrats are actively trying to do to undermine him.
sentences.zh: 总统所恐惧的正是民主党人正在积极试图破坏他的手段。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, Senator Schumer and even some of the House
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，舒默参议员甚至一些众议院

sentences.en: Democratic leaders have been name checking Mitch McConnell, the Senate majority leader all day, every day.
sentences.zh: 民主党领袖整天都在点名参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔。

sentences.en: Now, Leader McConnell has shown himself to be an adept negotiator during previous shutdowns.
sentences.zh: 现在，麦康奈尔领袖在之前的停摆中已经证明自己是一位娴熟的谈判者。

sentences.en: Why is he abdicating his responsibility now?
sentences.zh: 为什么他现在要放弃自己的责任？

sentences.en: Why is Leader McConnell shuffling off to the sidelines, pointing his fingers at everyone else and saying he won't be involved?
sentences.zh: 为什么麦康奈尔领袖要退居二线，指责其他人并声称自己不会参与？

sentences.en: Saying that McConnell needs to break with the president, marshal Republicans in the Senate to cut a deal with Democrats in the Senate to get this done.
sentences.zh: 他们说麦康奈尔需要与总统决裂，召集参议院的共和党人与参议院的民主党人达成协议，以解决这个问题。

sentences.en: The president needs intervention.
sentences.zh: 总统需要干预。

sentences.en: And Leader McConnell and Senate Republicans are just the right ones to intervene.
sentences.zh: 而麦康奈尔领袖和参议院共和党人正是最适合进行干预的人。

sentences.en: So it's true.
sentences.zh: 所以这是真的。

sentences.en: They have been trying to really drive a wedge among Republicans on this.
sentences.zh: 他们一直试图在共和党人之间打入楔子。

sentences.en: And if President
sentences.zh: 如果特朗普总统

sentences.en: Trump were to allow that to happen, his whole strategy here, which has been to just signal no willingness at all to compromise, would fall flat.
sentences.zh: 任由这种情况发生，他在这里的整个策略——即表现出完全不愿妥协的态度——就会彻底失败。

sentences.en: Mr. President, how much longer can this shutdown last?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，这次停摆还能持续多久？

sentences.en: And so he arrives at the Capitol, exits his limousine in the driveway, walks up the steps, walks through this whole phalanx of reporters all crowded around to see him.
sentences.zh: 于是他抵达国会大厦，从车道的豪华轿车里走出来，走上台阶，穿过一群围着他看的记者。

sentences.en: And somebody shouts at him.
sentences.zh: 有人对他大喊。

sentences.en: Mr. President, how much longer can this shutdown last?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，这次停摆还能持续多久？

sentences.en: We need border security.
sentences.zh: 我们需要边境安全。

sentences.en: We will have border security.
sentences.zh: 我们将会有边境安全。

sentences.en: Tremendous Republican support.
sentences.zh: 共和党给予了巨大的支持。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to win.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们会赢。

sentences.en: What's your message, you Republicans?
sentences.zh: 你对共和党人有什么话要说？

sentences.en: We need border security.
sentences.zh: 我们需要边境安全。

sentences.en: Very soon.
sentences.zh: 很快就会有。

sentences.en: How long do you want to let this shutdown last, Mr. President?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，你想让这次停摆持续多久？

sentences.en: Whatever it takes.
sentences.zh: 无论需要多久。

sentences.en: Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 总统先生。

sentences.en: And then he disappears behind closed doors into the Republican lunch.
sentences.zh: 然后他消失在紧闭的门后，进入了共和党午餐会。

sentences.en: And what does he say to these Republicans at the lunch?
sentences.zh: 他在午餐会上对这些共和党人说了什么？

sentences.en: Well, you might think that he'd be going in with like a
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能以为他会带着一套

sentences.en: very concise and firm set of talking points about the wall and the shutdown, but that's not what happens.
sentences.zh: 关于边境墙和停摆的非常简洁坚定的谈话要点进去，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: He goes in and gives what senators have told me was a very Trumpian sort of stream of consciousness,
sentences.zh: 他进去后发表了一番参议员们告诉我的、非常具有特朗普风格的意识流演讲，

sentences.en: 30 to 40 minute monologue about lots of other things having nothing to do with border security or the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 长达30到40分钟的独白，谈论了很多与边境安全或停摆毫无关系的事情。

sentences.en: He starts off with, we're doing so well.
sentences.zh: 他一开始就说，我们做得非常好。

sentences.en: Everything's great.
sentences.zh: 一切都很棒。

sentences.en: He's talking about jobs numbers.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了就业数据。

sentences.en: He's talking about his visit to Iraq over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了假期期间对伊拉克的访问。

sentences.en: He's joking with senators.
sentences.zh: 他与参议员们开玩笑。

sentences.en: And I mean, he's just all over the place, completely bouncing around.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他完全是东拉西扯，思绪跳跃。

sentences.en: And by the time he gets to border security and the wall, there's very little time for senators in the room to ask any questions.
sentences.zh: 等他谈到边境安全和边境墙时，房间里的参议员们几乎没有时间提问了。

sentences.en: And really his message is, this is my position.
sentences.zh: 他真正传达的信息是，这就是我的立场。

sentences.en: We need border security.
sentences.zh: 我们需要边境安全。

sentences.en: We need a wall.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一堵墙。

sentences.en: I'm not backing down.
sentences.zh: 我不会退缩。

sentences.en: The word I heard used most often by senators coming out of this meeting was resolute.
sentences.zh: 我听到参议员们在会议结束后最常使用的词是“坚定”。

sentences.en: He is not budging and you Republicans need to be behind me.
sentences.zh: 他不会让步，你们共和党人需要支持我。

sentences.en: We need to be united.
sentences.zh: 我们需要团结一致。

sentences.en: We're never going to get anywhere if we're not united.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不团结，我们将一事无成。

sentences.en: And he just keeps that up.
sentences.zh: 他一直在重复这些话。

sentences.en: A few of the senators who have expressed concerns publicly about this do so in the room.
sentences.zh: 几位公开表达过担忧的参议员在房间里也表达了看法。

sentences.en: Lisa Murkowski gets up and expresses her concerns.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·穆尔科斯基站起来表达了她的担忧。

sentences.en: She's worried about federal workers.
sentences.zh: 她担心联邦工作人员。

sentences.en: She really feels like the rest of the government can open up and we can still have this debate.
sentences.zh: 她确实觉得政府的其他部门可以重新开门，我们仍然可以进行这场辩论。

sentences.en: Susan Collins gets up.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·柯林斯站了起来。

sentences.en: She mentions the potential for a bipartisan deal that might involve giving legal status to the Dreamers.
sentences.zh: 她提到了达成两党协议的可能性，这可能涉及给予“追梦人”合法身份。

sentences.en: And what the president keeps on saying is just, I understand, but we just have to hang together here.
sentences.zh: 而总统一直说的是，我理解，但我们必须团结一致。

sentences.en: We have to be solid.
sentences.zh: 我们必须坚定。

sentences.en: You have to be behind me.
sentences.zh: 你们必须支持我。

sentences.en: This is my position.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的立场。

sentences.en: I'm not moving.
sentences.zh: 我不会动摇。

sentences.en: The Democrats are going to have to move.
sentences.zh: 民主党人将不得不让步。

sentences.en: And Senator John Kennedy from Louisiana said,
sentences.zh: 来自路易斯安那州的约翰·肯尼迪参议员说，

sentences.en: I'm not from Missouri, but he was like the Missouri mule who just sits down in the mud and says,
sentences.zh: 我不是密苏里人，但他就像那头坐在泥里说“我不会动”的密苏里骡子，

sentences.en: I'm not moving.
sentences.zh: 我不会动摇。

sentences.en: I would say that we have a very, very unified party.
sentences.zh: 我想说我们有一个非常、非常团结的政党。

sentences.en: Mitch has been fantastic.
sentences.zh: 米奇表现得太棒了。

sentences.en: Everybody in that room was fantastic.
sentences.zh: 房间里的每个人都表现得太棒了。

sentences.en: There was no reason for me even to be there.
sentences.zh: 我甚至没有理由去那里。

sentences.en: I knew that before we went.
sentences.zh: 在我们去之前我就知道了。

sentences.en: So what happens after this meeting?
sentences.zh: 那么会议结束后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the meeting breaks up and the president and the Republican leaders, as they almost always do after their weekly lunch,
sentences.zh: 嗯，会议结束了，总统和共和党领袖们像他们每周午餐会后几乎总是做的那样，

sentences.en: go out to the microphones and the assembled news cameras to make a short statement usually.
sentences.zh: 走到麦克风前和聚集的新闻摄像机前，通常会发表简短的声明。

sentences.en: And somewhat uncharacteristically,
sentences.zh: 有些不同寻常的是，

sentences.en: Senator Mitch McConnell, the majority leader, kind of hangs in the background while the president does most of the talking.
sentences.zh: 多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔在总统进行大部分发言时，一直站在背景中。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, We had a great meeting, we had a great time, actually.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我们开了一个很棒的会议，实际上我们度过了一段美好的时光。

sentences.en: There was no discussion about anything other than solidarity.
sentences.zh: 除了团结之外，没有讨论任何其他事情。

sentences.en: We had a great meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们开了一个很棒的会议。

sentences.en: You know, we didn't really talk about much other than that we're very united and we're all together.
sentences.zh: 你知道，除了我们非常团结并且我们都在一起之外，我们真的没有谈论太多其他事情。

sentences.en: And that was kind of the message.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是当时传达的信息。

sentences.en: And the Republican leadership didn't say much of anything.
sentences.zh: 而共和党领导层几乎什么都没说。

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell essentially followed that up with, you know, yeah, the president gave a pretty good description of what went on, like basically what he said.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔基本上接着说，你知道，是的，总统对发生的事情做了相当好的描述，基本上就是他所说的那样。

sentences.en: Which is, again, pretty rare for Mitch McConnell, who does not usually find himself at a loss for words after these meetings.
sentences.zh: 这对于米奇·麦康奈尔来说确实非常罕见，他通常在这些会议后不会无话可说。

sentences.en: He's usually pretty frank in his assessment.
sentences.zh: 他通常在评估时相当坦率。

sentences.en: But it was almost as if the Republicans had sort of ceded their territory to the president.
sentences.zh: 但给人的感觉几乎是共和党人已经把他们的地盘让给了总统。

sentences.en: Which tells you what exactly?
sentences.zh: 这到底说明了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think it tells me that the president has taken ownership of this in a way that's very public
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这说明总统以一种非常公开的方式承担了这件事的责任，

sentences.en: and that the Senate Republicans, frankly, at this point, kind of want him to own this because it's President Trump's demands, it's his strategy.
sentences.zh: 而且坦率地说，参议院共和党人在这一点上，某种程度上希望由他来承担，因为这是特朗普总统的要求，是他的策略。

sentences.en: They do not necessarily share these priorities, but they understand that their political fortunes are, for better or for worse, tied to his.
sentences.zh: 他们未必认同这些优先事项，但他们明白，无论好坏，他们的政治命运都与他捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: And if someone's going to make the case for why the Republicans in Congress are doing what they're doing,
sentences.zh: 如果有人要为国会共和党人为何这样做进行辩护，

sentences.en: it's going to be the president, who is, after all, the reason that they find themselves in this situation.
sentences.zh: 那肯定会是总统，毕竟，他们之所以陷入这种境地，原因就在于他。

sentences.en: But they can't forever escape their role, which is to legislate and fund the government and be held responsible for the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 但他们无法永远逃避自己的职责，即立法、为政府提供资金，并为政府停摆承担责任。

sentences.en: And so when the president at this lunch tells them, you must be unified, you must hold the line, you must stand with me, what is he offering them in return?
sentences.zh: 所以当总统在午餐会上告诉他们，你们必须团结一致，必须坚守阵地，必须支持我时，他能给他们什么回报呢？

sentences.en: And why do they seem so willing to do what he's asking in this moment when the shutdown may cost them politically and is certainly hurting their constituents?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们在这个时候看起来如此愿意听从他的要求，尽管政府停摆可能会让他们付出政治代价，而且肯定伤害了他们的选民？

sentences.en: I think it's not so much what he's offering as the implicit threat that if they are the one, two, three dozen Republicans
sentences.zh: 我认为与其说他提供了什么，不如说是一种隐含的威胁，即如果他们是那一两个、甚至几十个共和党人，

sentences.en: who somehow defect at this crucial point that he's going to declare them an enemy and then their political lives will be over.
sentences.zh: 在关键时刻倒戈，他就会宣布他们是敌人，那么他们的政治生涯就结束了。

sentences.en: But theoretically, Republicans could band together and simply decide that it's time to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 但从理论上讲，共和党人可以联合起来，简单地决定是时候重启政府了。

sentences.en: And that does not necessarily mean walking away from the wall.
sentences.zh: 这并不一定意味着放弃边境墙。

sentences.en: It simply means separating the issues out, as Senators Murkowski, Collins, Gardner are asking.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅意味着像穆尔科斯基、柯林斯、加德纳等参议员所要求的那样，将这些议题分开处理。

sentences.en: So why don't they do that?
sentences.zh: 那么他们为什么不这样做呢？

sentences.en: Well, for one thing, it doesn't seem like there's enough of them right now to reach a critical mass to do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，目前看来他们的人数似乎还不足以达到采取行动的临界点。

sentences.en: I mean, you would probably be talking about needing enough Republicans to band together with Democrats to produce 60 votes for something like that,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能需要足够的共和党人与民主党人联合起来，才能为类似的事情争取到60张选票，

sentences.en: which is what you need to get most things past the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这是在参议院通过大多数法案所需的票数。

sentences.en: But more to the point,
sentences.zh: 但更重要的一点是，

sentences.en: Senator Mitch McConnell is still the majority leader, and he has made it very clear that he has no intention of bringing up any legislation
sentences.zh: 参议员米奇·麦康奈尔仍然是多数党领袖，他已经非常明确地表示，他无意提出任何

sentences.en: that the president is not willing to sign.
sentences.zh: 总统不愿意签署的法案。

sentences.en: So there's no path for them to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有办法那样做。

sentences.en: If they were willing to use kind of guerrilla tactics on the Senate floor against their own party to try to attach amendments
sentences.zh: 如果他们愿意在参议院会议厅内针对本党采取某种游击战术，试图在麦康奈尔确实想要提出的各种法案中

sentences.en: to various pieces of legislation that McConnell does want to bring up or somehow try to make mischief in that way, there is a possibility they could do that.
sentences.zh: 附加修正案，或者以某种方式试图制造麻烦，他们是有可能做到的。

sentences.en: But that's not really what we're seeing from these senators.
sentences.zh: 但我们从这些参议员身上并没有真正看到这一点。

sentences.en: So what's clear is that, as the senators see it, the pain from this shutdown is not greater than the political risks involved in speaking out against the shutdown
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见的是，在参议员们看来，政府停摆带来的痛苦，并不比公开反对停摆

sentences.en: and breaking from this president.
sentences.zh: 并与总统决裂所涉及的政治风险更大。

sentences.en: I think that's true for the vast majority of Republicans right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对目前绝大多数共和党人来说都是如此。

sentences.en: So what happens after this news conference with the president and the Senate Republicans?
sentences.zh: 那么在总统和参议院共和党人的新闻发布会之后会发生什么？

sentences.en: The president leaves Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 总统离开了国会大厦。

sentences.en: He goes back to the White House where he has invited the bipartisan congressional leadership, including the Democrats, to another of these meetings in the Situation Room.
sentences.zh: 他回到白宫，邀请了包括民主党人在内的两党国会领导层，在战情室举行了另一场会议。

sentences.en: This is now the third time they've all gathered there to try to hash this out.
sentences.zh: 这是他们第三次聚在那里试图解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And nobody really knew what to expect from this meeting.
sentences.zh: 没人知道这次会议会有什么结果。

sentences.en: Well, it sounds like from what you've said that there's not a whole lot of optimism that something's going to happen because the president has just told Senate Republicans,
sentences.zh: 嗯，听你刚才说的，似乎大家对会有什么进展并不抱太大希望，因为总统刚刚告诉参议院共和党人，

sentences.en: stand behind me and let's not budge at all.
sentences.zh: 支持我，我们绝不让步。

sentences.en: That doesn't seem like a constructive approach to the beginning of the talks.
sentences.zh: 这看起来不是一个建设性的谈判开端。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the Democrats also have spent the morning, you know, having a news conference with furloughed federal workers saying, we will never give in to a wall.
sentences.zh: 而且民主党人也花了一上午时间，你知道，和被迫休假的联邦工作人员开了个新闻发布会，说我们绝不会在边境墙问题上屈服。

sentences.en: Look at how this is hurting the average American.
sentences.zh: 看看这对普通美国人造成了多大的伤害。

sentences.en: Why can't we just reopen the government?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能直接重启政府呢？

sentences.en: So everyone is in their corner and it's not clear what headway can be made in this meeting.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都各持己见，这次会议能取得什么进展尚不清楚。

sentences.en: But in fact, even by the standards of these negotiations up till now, which have not been very productive, the meeting this afternoon was, like, way, way worse
sentences.zh: 但事实上，即使按照迄今为止这些并不怎么有效的谈判标准来看，今天下午的会议也简直是糟糕透顶，

sentences.en: because, I mean, it hardly even got started.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，会议几乎还没开始就结束了。

sentences.en: It was basically, the president started out the meeting handing out candy, apparently.
sentences.zh: 基本上，总统在会议开始时分发了糖果，显然是这样。

sentences.en: I guess as a gesture of goodwill or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是一种善意的姿态之类的。

sentences.en: But after they got over their pleasantries,
sentences.zh: 但在他们寒暄过后，

sentences.en: basically the president and vice president Pence, who was also there, wanted to know why Democrats hadn't come to the table with a counteroffer.
sentences.zh: 基本上总统和同样在场的副总统彭斯想知道为什么民主党人没有带着还价方案来到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: They said, you know, we gave you an offer, which was $5.7 billion for a wall.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，我们给了你们一个方案，即57亿美元用于建墙。

sentences.en: You said no, but so what's your counteroffer?
sentences.zh: 你们拒绝了，那么你们的还价是什么？

sentences.en: And once again, Nancy Pelosi and Chuck Schumer say, well, we don't have a counteroffer and we will continue not to have a counteroffer for as long as the government remains closed.
sentences.zh: 南希·佩洛西和查克·舒默再次表示，好吧，我们没有还价方案，只要政府继续关闭，我们就不会有还价方案。

sentences.en: You need to reopen the government, then we can talk about border security.
sentences.zh: 你们需要重启政府，然后我们才能谈论边境安全问题。

sentences.en: And so President Trump finally turns to Nancy Pelosi and says, okay, Nancy, if I were to agree to quickly reopen the government, would you reach an agreement with me within 30 days
sentences.zh: 于是特朗普总统终于转向南希·佩洛西说，好吧，南希，如果我同意尽快重启政府，你会在30天内与我达成协议

sentences.en: to fund the wall?
sentences.zh: 为边境墙提供资金吗？

sentences.en: And she says, no.
sentences.zh: 她说，不。

sentences.en: The Democrats' position has been no, no, no money for a wall.
sentences.zh: 民主党的立场一直都是不，不，绝不为边境墙拨款。

sentences.en: We will not agree to a wall.
sentences.zh: 我们不会同意建墙。

sentences.en: And he just stands up and he says, bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 然后他直接站起来说，再见。

sentences.en: And he walks out.
sentences.zh: 他走了出去。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He just ends the negotiation.
sentences.zh: 他直接结束了谈判。

sentences.en: He just gets up and leaves.
sentences.zh: 他起身就走了。

sentences.en: Cold out here.
sentences.zh: 外面很冷。

sentences.en: It's cold out here and the temperature wasn't much warmer in the Situation Room.
sentences.zh: 外面很冷，战情室里的气氛也没暖和多少。

sentences.en: Our meeting did not last long.
sentences.zh: 我们的会议没持续多久。

sentences.en: And, you know, as you can imagine, the Democrats came out and went straight to the microphones.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以想象，民主党人出来后直接走向了麦克风。

sentences.en: He sort of slammed the table.
sentences.zh: 他拍了桌子。

sentences.en: And when Leader Pelosi said she didn't agree with the wall, he just walked out and said, we have nothing to discuss.
sentences.zh: 当佩洛西领袖说她不同意建墙时，他直接走出去说，我们没什么可谈的。

sentences.en: So he said it was a waste of his time.
sentences.zh: 所以他说这是在浪费他的时间。

sentences.en: So we're sort of right back to where we were before.
sentences.zh: 所以我们又回到了原点。

sentences.en: So in the past, we've described this situation as kind of an impasse.
sentences.zh: 过去我们把这种情况描述为一种僵局。

sentences.en: I would say at this point, it also looks like a kind of breakdown in the negotiations.
sentences.zh: 我想说在这一点上，这看起来也像是谈判的一种破裂。

sentences.en: When it comes to the Republicans and this lunch and the message from the president about unity,
sentences.zh: 谈到共和党人和这次午餐会，以及总统关于团结的信息，

sentences.en: I can't help thinking about what Republican Senator Lindsey Graham said a few nights ago in a television interview that seems to help explain this approach.
sentences.zh: 我不禁想起共和党参议员林赛·格雷厄姆几天前在电视采访中所说的话，这似乎有助于解释这种做法。

sentences.en: To my Republican colleagues, this is the best chance we'll ever have to help President Trump get border wall funding, still barrier funding, and at the same time fix the loopholes.
sentences.zh: 对于我的共和党同僚们，这是我们有史以来帮助特朗普总统获得边境墙资金、获得屏障资金，同时修补漏洞的最佳机会。

sentences.en: The only way we lose is to give in.
sentences.zh: 我们输的唯一方式就是屈服。

sentences.en: If we'll stand firm, put deals on the table that make sense, we will win this on behalf of the American people.
sentences.zh: 如果我们立场坚定，提出合理的交易方案，我们将代表美国人民赢得这场胜利。

sentences.en: But if we undercut the president, that's the end of his presidency and the end of our party.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们削弱总统，那就是他总统任期的终结，也是我们党的终结。

sentences.en: And we deserve to be punished if we give in now.
sentences.zh: 如果我们现在屈服，我们活该受到惩罚。

sentences.en: What do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: I mean, it's an interesting statement.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个有趣的声明。

sentences.en: All I could think of when he made it was it sounded like a group of people, Republicans, who've essentially kind of gotten in this bus that's hurtling toward a cliff
sentences.zh: 当他说出这番话时，我唯一能想到的是，这听起来像是一群人，共和党人，他们基本上已经坐上了一辆正冲向悬崖的巴士，

sentences.en: and like can't get off it now because we're already on the bus, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且因为已经在车上了，现在没法下车了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And I think that's in some ways privately the sentiment that a lot of Republicans have, which is that, you know, this is really bad.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，私下里很多共和党人都有这种情绪，那就是，你知道，这真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: This is not sort of the ground they want to stake out.
sentences.zh: 这并不是他们想要坚守的阵地。

sentences.en: But Trump is the leader of the party.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普是党的领袖。

sentences.en: He's the president.
sentences.zh: 他是总统。

sentences.en: He's shut down the government.
sentences.zh: 他关闭了政府。

sentences.en: He's done his first ever address to the nation from the Oval Office.
sentences.zh: 他在椭圆形办公室发表了有史以来第一次全国讲话。

sentences.en: I mean, he is using all of the tools of the presidency on this one issue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他正在利用总统职权的所有工具来处理这一个问题。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's overstating things to say that if he can't deliver this in some way, shape or fashion that satisfies those voters, he will have a hard time being reelected.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果他不能以某种方式、某种形式兑现承诺来满足那些选民，他将很难连任，这并不夸张。

sentences.en: And Republicans could have a hard time trying to ride his or anyone else's coattails.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人在试图搭他的顺风车或任何人的顺风车时，可能会遇到困难。

sentences.en: And in that case, if Republicans see this as essentially an existential issue for all of them, for the president, for themselves, for the whole party, then there's no incentive
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，如果共和党人认为这本质上是关系到他们所有人、总统、他们自己以及整个党派存亡的问题，那么就没有动力

sentences.en: to end the shutdown and to walk away from the wall, which suggests that this is going to be, in fact, a very long shutdown, even if a few Republicans are starting to break from
sentences.zh: 去结束停摆并放弃边境墙，这表明这实际上将是一场非常漫长的停摆，即使少数共和党人开始与

sentences.en: the president.
sentences.zh: 总统决裂。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为你说得对。

sentences.en: This is bigger than just a few people.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是几个人的问题。

sentences.en: This is about the president and his party.
sentences.zh: 这是关于总统和他所在的党派。

sentences.en: And it's also the case that there's very little disincentive for Democrats to continue on the path that they're on.
sentences.zh: 而且民主党人继续走他们目前的道路也几乎没有什么负面激励。

sentences.en: Their base is very happy with them saying, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 他们的基本盘对他们说绝对不，感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: If Trump wants this wall, say no.
sentences.zh: 如果特朗普想要这堵墙，就说不。

sentences.en: They have no trouble sustaining that argument among Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他们在民主党人中维持这一论点毫无困难。

sentences.en: And frankly, among a growing amount of independents.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，在越来越多的独立选民中也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the wall is not popular.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，边境墙并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: And shutting down the government for a wall is even less popular.
sentences.zh: 而为了建墙而关闭政府更不受欢迎。

sentences.en: So they're on solid ground as well, which makes it very difficult to see how either side budges.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也处于稳固的立场，这使得双方都很难做出让步。

sentences.en: And as of Friday, we'll be on day 21 of this shutdown, which will make it tied for the longest in American history.
sentences.zh: 截至周五，我们将进入这次停摆的第21天，这将使其并列成为美国历史上最长的一次停摆。

sentences.en: And I don't have any trouble imagining that it's going to go much, much longer than that.
sentences.zh: 而且我完全可以想象它会持续得比这长得多。

sentences.en: Julie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 朱莉，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Wednesday evening, eight Republican House members broke with President Trump by voting
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，八名共和党众议员通过投票与特朗普总统决裂，

sentences.en: for Democratic legislation that would reopen the government without funding the border wall.
sentences.zh: 支持民主党的立法，该立法将在不为边境墙提供资金的情况下重启政府。

sentences.en: But with the majority of Senate Republicans standing by the president, the legislation has no path to passage.
sentences.zh: 但由于大多数参议院共和党人支持总统，该法案没有通过的途径。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间去探索付费墙后的内容，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein, who appointed the special counsel
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，任命特别检察官并多次成为特朗普总统愤怒目标的副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦，

sentences.en: and has been the repeated target of President Trump's rage, will step down as soon as the president appoints a new attorney general.
sentences.zh: 将在总统任命新司法部长后立即离职。

sentences.en: Rosenstein started off as a Trump ally by writing the memo used to fire FBI Director James Comey,
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦最初通过撰写用于解雇联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米的备忘录，成为了特朗普的盟友，

sentences.en: but quickly became a foe, who suggested secretly recording Trump in the White House to expose the
sentences.zh: 但很快就变成了敌人，他曾建议在白宫秘密录下特朗普的谈话以揭露他政府的混乱，

sentences.en: chaos of his administration, and who discussed the possibility of recruiting cabinet members to invoke the 25th Amendment to remove Trump from office.
sentences.zh: 并讨论了招募内阁成员援引第25修正案将特朗普免职的可能性。

sentences.en: Rosenstein will leave his post after the Senate approves a permanent replacement for his previous boss, Jeff Sessions.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦将在参议院批准他前任老板杰夫·塞申斯的永久继任者后离职。

sentences.en: A candidate for that job, William Barr, who was the attorney general under President George
sentences.zh: 该职位的候选人威廉·巴尔，曾是乔治·H·W·布什总统任内的司法部长，

sentences.en: H.W.
sentences.zh: 将于下周开始他的参议院确认听证会。

sentences.en: Bush, will begin his Senate confirmation hearings next week.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日》的全部内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。
